To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Planck 2013 data constrain variations in the fine structure "constant", α, to Δα/ α < 4.0 × 10-5 and in the electron mass, me, to Δme/me < 1.5 × 10-4 at the 95% confidence level, and that the data are consistent with a constant α and me over the history of the Universe.
we have improved the constraint on a possible time variation of the fundamental constants α and me by a factor of 2-4, and that the spatial variation of α is constrained to be < 3%.
Planck has improved the constraint on the variation of the fine-structure constant by a factor of 2.5 compared to the WMAP data alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of fundamental physical constants and their possible variations.
the search for the possible variation of the fundamental constants of nature.
the study of variations in fundamental constants, and we have used the Planck data to constrain these variations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Planck results are fully compatible with the constancy of the fundamental physical constants within the precision of the measurements.
the Planck results do not show any evidence of a variation of α or of me.
there is no evidence for a variation in fundamental constants, neither in time nor in space, at the precision level of these observations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have improved the constraints on the fundamental constants by a factor 3-5 compared to WMA, but the results are still compatible within 1σ.
we have been able to improve the constraint of α by about a factor 5 compared to the previous results from WMAP.
Planck is able to improve the constraints on the variation in fundamental constants by a factor 5 compared to previous data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Planck 2013 data provide a significant improvement on the limits on the variation of the fundamental constants, compared to the previous CMB data, as well on the limits on a dipole variation of α.

, in spite of the fact that the cosmological data alone are not very constraining for variations in fundamental constants, they do provide a very valuable complementary constraint to laboratory experiments and astrophysical observations.
the current Planck data allow us to set the most stringent constraints to date on the time and spatial variations of α.
